text: In the beginning, the Word was with God. The Word was also God. He was with God at the beginning.
notes: The Greek word 'logos' is translated as 'Word.' It means God's message and teaching. It's a special way to talk about Jesus. The phrase 'was with God' emphasizes Jesus' close relationship with God. We chose a simple, repetitive structure to help kids understand the important idea: Jesus was with God from the very start.

text: He was in the beginning with God.
notes: The Greek word 'arch' means 'with' or 'at the beginning.' The phrase 'in the beginning with God' is a traditional and conservative rendering of this verse. It emphasizes Jesus' eternal relationship with God.

text: Everything came from him. Nothing was made without him. All things were made through him.
notes: The Greek phrase 'di autou' and 'cwriv autou' can be interpreted in different ways. Here, I chose a rendering emphasizing 'through him' and 'without him' to convey the idea of God's active involvement in creation. This is a conservative rendering that aligns with traditional interpretations of the verse.

text: The Word was life. And this life was the light for people.
notes: The Greek phrase 'en autw' can mean 'in him' or 'with him.' Here, 'the Word was life' is a more straightforward rendering. 'Zwh' is translated as 'life.' 'Fwv' is translated as 'light.' 'Twn anyrwpwn' is translated as 'for people.'

text: The light shines in the darkness. The darkness did not understand it.
notes: The Greek phrase 'to fwv' is genitive, referring to 'the light.' The verb 'fainei' means 'shines.' The darkness 'ou katelaben' means 'did not understand.' A more literal translation could be 'did not grasp,' but 'understand' is simpler for children. This verse speaks of Jesus, the light, coming into the world. It's a very important verse about God's love.

text: There was a man. God sent him. His name was John.
notes: The Greek word 'egeneto' means 'there was' or 'became.' I chose 'there was' for simplicity. 'Apestalmenov' means 'sent.' It indicates God chose and sent John. 'Iwannhv' is the name John.

text: He told them why he came. He wanted them to share about the light. He hoped everyone would believe because of him.
notes: The Greek word 'marturian' means 'testimony.' I used 'told them why he came' to convey this idea simply. 'Fwtov' means 'the light,' referring to Jesus. 'Pantev' means 'everyone.' The phrase 'di autou' means 'through him,' emphasizing Jesus' role in bringing people to faith.

text: He was not the Light, but to show people the Light.
notes: The Greek phrase 'marturhsh peri' can mean 'to testify about' or 'to show'. I chose 'to show' as it's more accessible for children and aligns with the verse's overall message of revealing the Light. The original text emphasizes John's role as a witness, pointing to Jesus as the Light.
The word 'Light' refers to Jesus, who brings God's truth and goodness into the world.

text: The light shines on everyone. It comes into the world. The light gives life to all people.
notes: The Greek word 'alhyinon' is tricky. It can mean 'light' or 'world.' Here, 'world' felt too big for young readers. We chose 'everyone' to focus on people. 'Fwtizei' means 'shines' or 'gives light.' We used 'gives life' to make it easier to understand. 'Eiv' means 'into.'

text: In the beginning, the world was made. The world was made through him. But the world did not know him.
notes: The Greek phrase 'en tw kosmw' is a bit tricky. It can mean 'in the world' or 'with the world.' Here, I chose 'In the beginning, the world was made' to keep it simple and focus on creation. 'Di autou' means 'through him,' so I used that phrase. 'Ouk egnw' means 'did not know.' It's often used to mean a lack of understanding or recognition, not just a lack of information.

text: He came to his own people. But his own people did not welcome him.
notes: The Greek word 'idios' can mean 'own' in different ways. Here, it refers to the Jewish people, who were expected to receive the Messiah. The phrasing 'did not welcome him' is a simple way to convey the rejection described in the original text. A more literal translation might be 'did not receive him,' but 'welcome' is more accessible to children.

text: But those who believed received the right to become children of God. They became children because they trusted in His name.
notes: The Greek word 'genesyai' means 'to become' or 'to be born.' Here, it means to become children of God through faith. This is a spiritual birth, not a physical one. The phrase 'trusted in His name' is a simple way to explain the concept of faith in Jesus.
The verb 'edwken' (gave) is used to convey the idea that God gives this authority. It's a generous gift.

text: They weren't born from human parents. They weren't born from human desire. God was their Father.
notes: The original Greek uses a complex sentence structure. I broke it into three shorter sentences for clarity. 'Desire' is used to represent 'yelhmatov androv' to avoid potentially confusing vocabulary for the target audience. The phrase 'God was their Father' is a simplified rendering of 'ek yeou egennhyhsan' to convey the idea of divine origin in an accessible way. This verse speaks of Jesus and the Holy Spirit, who are not born in the usual way.

text: The Word became human. He lived among us. We saw his glory. It was like the glory of God's only Son. He was full of grace and truth.
notes: The Greek word 'logos' is translated as 'Word' here, referring to Jesus. 'Sarx' means 'flesh,' indicating Jesus took on human form. 'Alhyeiav' is translated as 'truth,' a key concept in John's Gospel. The phrase 'monogenouv para patrov' is a complex one. It means 'only Son from the Father.' We've simplified it to 'God's only Son' for clarity. The original Greek uses 'eyeasameya' which is difficult to translate simply. We chose 'we saw' to convey the idea of witnessing his glory.

text: I tell about Him. I heard the Father say, 'This is My Son.' He came after me. He was before me. He is my first!
notes: The original Greek uses a complex sentence structure. I broke it into shorter sentences for easier understanding. 'Prwtov mou hn' can mean 'He was my first' or 'He is my first.' I chose 'He is my first' as it emphasizes Jesus' eternal nature, which is a key theological point. This is a conservative rendering.

text: From God’s fullness, we all receive. We get grace instead of grace.
notes: The original Greek uses 'carin anti caritov,' which is a bit unusual. It seems to mean that we receive God’s grace instead of needing anything else. I chose a simple way to say this to make it easy for kids to understand. Some scholars think it means we receive grace for grace, but that is a more complex idea.

text: God gave Moses the law. Through Jesus Christ, grace and truth came.
notes: The Greek word 'cariv' is translated as 'grace.' It means God's kindness to us. 'Alhyeia' is translated as 'truth.' It means being honest and real. The verse connects the Old Testament law with the New Testament grace and truth found in Jesus.

text: Before time began, the only Son was with God. He was close to the Father. He showed us God’s glory.
notes: The Greek word 'pwpote' can mean 'before time' or 'at first.' We chose 'before time' for clarity with children. 'Monogenhv uiov' is often translated as 'only Son.' We used 'only Son' to emphasize Jesus' unique relationship with God. 'Exhghsato' means 'declared' or 'showed.' We chose 'showed' as a simpler and more engaging word for children.

text: John told about Jesus. Jewish leaders came from Jerusalem. They were priests and teachers. They asked Jesus, 'Who are you?'
He confessed. He didn't fear. He said, 'I am not the Christ.'
They asked him, “Are you the promised one?” He said, “I am not.”
Then Jesus asked them, “Why do you ask me this? What do others say about me?”
He told them, 'Repent! Turn to the LORD.' This is what Isaiah the prophet said.
Some people were sent from the Pharisees.
They asked Jesus, “Why do you baptize people? Are you the Messiah? Or are you Elijah? Or the prophet?”
John answered, “I baptize you with water. But someone more powerful will come. You don’t know him now.
He who comes after me is greater than I. I am not worthy to untie his sandals.
Then Jesus came from Galilee. He came to the Jordan River. John was there, baptizing people.
The next day, John saw Jesus coming. John said, “Look! This is the Lamb of God. He takes away the sins of the world.”
He said, 'Someone is coming after me. He was already before me. He is the most important person.'
I didn't come to judge people. I came to show Israel God's way. That's why I was baptized in water.
John said, “I saw the Spirit come down from heaven! It looked like a dove and stayed on Him.”

John said, “I baptize with water. But someone else will baptize you with the Holy Spirit.” He told me this. The Spirit will come down. It will stay on them. That person will baptize with the Holy Spirit.
I saw him! I told everyone he is God’s Son.
The next day, John was there again. Two of his followers were with him.
Philip found Jesus walking nearby. He said, 'Look, the Lamb of God!'
Two of his followers heard him. They started following Jesus.
Then Jesus asked the people following Him. He said, “What are you looking for?” They replied, “Teacher, we heard you were here. We want to know where you live.”
He told them, 'Stay here and look after him.' They saw where he lived. They stayed with him that day. It was about the tenth hour.
Then Andrew, Simon Peter’s brother, heard this. He followed Jesus. The two men who heard John also followed Jesus.
Philip found him first. He was Nathanael’s brother. Philip said, “We found the Messiah! He is the one Moses wrote about in the law.”
They brought him to Jesus. Jesus asked, “What is your name?” He said, “Simon, son of John.” Jesus said, “You will be called Peter.”
notes: Peter means 'rock' in Greek.

text: The next day, Jesus went to Galilee. He found Philip. Jesus said, “Come follow me!”
Philip was from Bethsaida. He was a town near the Sea of Galilee. Andrew and Peter knew him.
Philip found Nathanael. He said, “Moses wrote about you in the law. Also, the prophets talked about Jesus, the Son of Joseph from Nazareth.”
Philip, John said, 'Nathanael from Nazareth can do good things!' Philip replied, 'Come and see!'
Jesus saw Nathan coming. He said about him, 'Look! A true Israelite! There is no trick in him.'
Philip asked Jesus a question. Jesus answered, 'I saw you under the fig tree.'
He asked, 'Teacher, are you the Son of God? Are you the King of Israel?'
Jesus answered him. He said, “What I told you, believe it! Seeing is not as important as trusting me.”
Jesus said, “Truly, truly, I tell you. You will see heaven open. You will see God’s angels going up and down to the Son of Man.”
